reference_bounds.method: ICL mode, --trim-seconds N against the upstream clone.wav (8.08 s / 193920 samples at 24 kHz). N <= 8.08 s truncates the clip; N > 8.08 s loops it (tile then truncate) rather than sourcing new audio, since the clip is shorter than the 10 s and 30 s points this measurement needed. Same target text, language, and seed for every duration, so frame-count differences are attributable to the reference duration alone.

reference_clip.ref_text: Okay. Yeah. I resent you. I love you. I respect you. But you know what? You blew it! And thanks to you.

reference_bounds.target_text: This is a test of Qwen three T T S base voice cloning.

baseline_full_clip.note: Same case, run with no --trim-seconds (the full 8.08 s clip). This is the build/goldens/qwen3-tts/qwen3-tts-12hz-0-6b-base/base-icl-en case.

measurements.intelligibility_basis: Not perceptually judged -- no audio playback capability in this environment. Objective signals only: peak_abs and rms are in the same range as every other measurement here (not silence); distinct_semantic_codes/generated_code_frames = 0.79, comparable to the baseline's 0.93, so this is not the family's documented single-repeated-code degeneracy. The frame count is 3.0x the 45-frame baseline for the identical text and seed, which is an anomaly worth a real listening pass before being called usable.

Not perceptually judged. distinct_semantic_codes/generated_code_frames = 0.79 (vs. baseline 0.93) and peak/rms are unremarkable, so no silence or single-code lock. Frame count is 2.8x the 45-frame baseline -- the same length anomaly as 0.5 s, smaller in degree. This is the plan's current provisional min_frames_per_clip (24000 samples); the anomaly here is the reason this document does not simply confirm that bound.

Not perceptually judged. distinct_semantic_codes/generated_code_frames = 0.79, peak/rms unremarkable -- no silence or single-code lock. Frame count is 2.5x the 45-frame baseline: the same over-length pattern as 0.5 s and 1 s, attenuating as reference duration grows toward the clip's native 8.08 s.

Not perceptually judged. Frame count (42) lands within 3 frames of the 45-frame baseline, and distinct_semantic_codes/generated_code_frames = 0.88, close to baseline's 0.93 -- no anomaly by these signals. This duration needed the clip looped 2x (8.08 s native < 10 s requested), so the reference audio is not natural continuous speech at this length; that is a property of the measurement method, not of the model.

Not perceptually judged. peak/rms are unremarkable (not silence) and 8 of 9 frames hold distinct codes (not a single-code lock), so this is not the family's documented degeneracy pattern either. But 9 frames (0.72 s) is far too short to plausibly contain the 11-word target sentence that took 45 frames (3.6 s) at the clip's native length -- the opposite anomaly from the short-reference cases (premature termination/truncation rather than running long). Also needed the clip looped 4x, so it is not natural continuous speech at this length either.

flags: 0.5 s, 1 s, and 3 s reference durations each produced 2.5x-3.0x the 45-frame baseline generated-code-frame count for the same target text and seed. None show the family's documented single-repeated-code degeneracy (docs/porting/families/qwen3-tts.md's greedy trap), and none look like silence by peak/rms, but the length anomaly itself was not perceptually verified as usable speech.

30 s reference (clip looped 4x) produced only 9 generated frames (0.72 s) for a sentence that needs ~45 frames at the clip's native length -- looks like premature termination or a clipped utterance rather than a silence/single-code failure. Not perceptually verified.
10 s reference (clip looped 2x) landed within 3 frames of the baseline and shows no anomaly by these signals -- the best-behaved of the five points measured.

10 s and 30 s both required looping the 8.08 s clip to reach the requested duration (this clip is shorter than both points), so those two measurements describe the model's response to *repeated* audio at that duration, not necessarily to natural continuous speech of that length.
reference_bounds.recommendation: Neither edge of the plan's provisional min_frames_per_clip=24000 (1 s) / max_frames_per_clip=720000 (30 s) bounds shows this family's known hard-failure signature (near-silence or a single code dominating the output), so this measurement does not by itself demand narrowing them. But 1 s's 2.8x frame-count anomaly and 30 s's abrupt 9-frame undershoot are both real signals that something about generation quality changes at the edges, and this agent has no capability to judge whether the resulting audio is actually usable speech. Per this project's own practice (offer the listening pass before shipping), Task 6 should not treat these bounds as validated from this report alone -- a human listening pass on the 0.5 s/1 s/30 s renders under build/qwen3-tts-reference-bounds/ is owed before either bound is shipped as more than provisional.
